title: Browser-local tools
description: Add a local browser tool to JSON Pages without a separate HTML document or server.

cells.text: A `local-tool` element mounts trusted site JavaScript inside a normal JSON Page. EdgePress owns the document, theme, navigation, page rows, escaping and asset fingerprints. Use this element for local calculators, file readers or search tools; external providers still require a consent-controlled service.

cells.code:
{
  "type": "local-tool",
  "id": "question-search",
  "title": "Search the question bank",
  "script": "/tools/search.js",
  "stylesheet": "/tools/search.css",
  "data": "/data/questions.json",
  "fallback": "Enable JavaScript to search locally."
}

cells.text: Put executable assets in `static/` or `content/assets/`. All referenced assets must exist at build time. Scripts use `.js` or `.mjs`, optional styles use `.css`, and optional public data uses `.json`. Paths must be local absolute site paths without traversal, query strings or remote origins. Keep IDs unique within the Page.

The tool module is trusted source, with the same responsibility as a theme script. Keep private files and inputs in browser memory, load expensive workers or models on visitor demand, and provide cancellation and clear failures. A local element does not authorize requests to external services or add an API. Static JSON remains refreshable; executable dependencies receive immutable hashed URLs.
